function: Distributed multi-agent RL control of UAV motion, ISAC transmit power and uplink channel allocation, maximising effective mutual information and users served (p. 1, p. 7).
system: Two antennas per UAV: directional for ISAC, omnidirectional to the BS; no RIS; 3 GHz carrier, 5 MHz uplink, 0.1 MHz ISAC band (p. 3; Table I, p. 11).
method: RMADDPG-DDA: MADDPG with random network distillation and dynamic data augmentation, MLP actor and critic; multi-agent reinforcement learning, centralized training, decentralized execution (p. 8, p. 9).
data_channel: Own simulation: probabilistic LoS path loss to BS, free-space LoS ISAC links, 40 vehicles at a crossroad; no 3GPP or measured data (p. 4, p. 5, p. 11).
test_conditions: 400 training episodes, 4 UAVs, 40 vehicles; tested in 10 runs of the same environment; other UAV counts and energy weights are retrained, not transferred (p. 11, p. 12).
baselines: MADDPG, DDPG and multi-agent SAC (MASAC), all learned; no non-learned baseline (p. 12).
metrics: Average training reward, effective mutual information, users served, constraint margins (communication SNR, data capacity, UAV spacing), UAV energy consumption (p. 12, p. 13).
complexity: Order of complexity of Algorithm 1 in episodes, steps, UAVs, batch size, network input dimensions and hidden neurons, Eq. (47), p. 11; no FLOPs or runtime.
q1_support: p. 4: "communication between UAVs and BS is described as a probabilistic path loss model". Custom model (constants a, b in Table I, p. 11); the ISAC links are assumed LoS and free space (p. 5). No 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 12: "We performed 10 parallel tests." These runs use the same environment; p. 12: "we train RMADDPG-DDA models with different numbers of UAVs and test them", so each UAV count is trained afresh, not transferred.
q3_support: p. 12: "as baselines, such as MADDPG, DDPG, and multi-agent SAC (MASAC)". All three are learned; Figs. 5 to 9 compare no non-learned method (random, fixed or optimization-based), and p. 14: "significantly outperformed traditional baselines" names no other method.
q4_support: p. 11: "The complexity of Algorithm 1 can be approximately expressed as" the order given in Eq. (47).
q5_support: p. 11: "the deep learning framework is exploited based on TensorFlow". No code or data link or DOI is given; all data come from the authors' own simulator (p. 11), with no public dataset.
notes: Area 6, not 5: the learned MARL controls UAV motion, ISAC transmit power and uplink channel allocation of an aerial ISAC link (p. 7, Eq. 20), and area 6 outranks area 5 when both fit. If the reviewer assigns area 5, the work falls under system (single-antenna links without RIS: p. 3, one directional and one omnidirectional antenna per UAV; p. 14: "Given the sensing limitations of the single antenna"). UAV trajectory is above the physical layer, but it is learned jointly with transmit power and channel allocation, so above_phy does not apply. The UAV-BS channel is the probabilistic LoS model with constants a and b taken from [15] (p. 4), not a standardized model, so q1 is 0. q4 rests on the O(...) expression of Eq. (47) for Algorithm 1 (p. 11).
